ranked.label: discovered meaning

neighbours.label: declared is brittle, discovered is resilient

ranked.anchor: fact-anchored: a quote in §Meaning Is Not Declared — It Is Discovered
ranked.def: Meaning determined by traversing a node's edges.
ranked.section: Meaning Is Not Declared — It Is Discovered
ranked.quote: In a graph-first system, meaning is discovered: "This node has edges to other nodes. By traversing those edges, we can determine what this node relates to, what constraints apply, and how confidently we can characterise it."

ranked.label: declared meaning

neighbours.label: declared is brittle, discovered is resilient

ranked.anchor: fact-anchored: a quote in §Meaning Is Not Declared — It Is Discovered
ranked.def: Meaning asserted by a schema, which instances conform to or fail.
ranked.section: Meaning Is Not Declared — It Is Discovered
ranked.quote: In a schema-first system, meaning is declared: "This object IS a Task. It HAS these fields. Its status MUST be one of these values." The schema is the authority, and instances conform or fail validation.

ranked.label: meaning thins measurably at boundaries
ranked.anchor: fact-anchored: a quote in §Meaning Is Not Declared — It Is Discovered
ranked.def: Crossing a boundary thins meaning rather than breaking it, and the system can report exactly how thin.
ranked.section: Meaning Is Not Declared — It Is Discovered
ranked.quote: it just means some edges don't extend across that boundary, and the meaning becomes thinner (less confident) on the other side
